Sinus arrhythmia

Some variation in sinoatrial node discharge rate is common, normally it should be less than 120 ms (3 small squares in ECG paper) between the longest and shortest P-P interval

Sinus arrhythmia is when the variation exceeds 120 ms

ECG characteristics of sinus arrhythmia include:

Normal sinus P waves (P wave is monoform and in pattern consistent it originating from the sinus node) and PR interval

1:1 atrioventricular conduction (AV conduction)

Variation of at least 120 ms between the shortest and longest P – P interval

Occasional junctional escape beats maybe present during very long P-P interval

No treatment is required

Sinus arrhythmias are affected primarily by respiration (because during respiration, intermittent vagus nerve activation occurs, which result in beat-to-beat variation in the resting heart rate)

Sinus arrhythmia commonly found in children and young adults, disappearing with advancing age

It indicates good cardiovascular health

Presentation

Sinus arrhythmia is an incidental finding on ECGs

Rarely it may lead to symptoms like SOB and palpitation

DDx

If two or more different P waves morphologies are present then atrial ectopy, wandering atrial pacemaker or another competing non sinus focus maybe present
